source.original_title: 05/13/2026 - Marc Moub & Harry Edmonds KFS- Kettlebell Body Game Plan Session
source.display_title: 05/13/2026 - Marc Moub & Harry Edmonds KFS- Kettlebell Body Game Plan Session — Follow Up

setter.name: Kim Forbes-Sobers
setter.evidence: Rep: 'I know you spoke with Kim. He kind of gave me a little bit of a head start on you.' Prospect later confirms she has already contacted him on WhatsApp: 'you, him has already pinged me on it, yeah.'

prospect.name: Marc Moubarak
prospect.family_status: Has a young child — 'we have a little one, so my free time is reduced tremendously' and ended the call for 'my daddy activities'
prospect.training_background: Former CrossFitter — says it caused injuries through too much intensity and poor attention to form. Then bodybuilding-style gym training, which he says produced progressive stiffness. Also did a lot of yoga, which he found insufficient as a workout. Started kettlebells a few days before the call, training at home in a compact space early in the morning, and likes circuit-style work for the cardiovascular and stress-flushing effect.
prospect.medical: Active, interlinked spinal and hip pain. Kettlebell swings are currently producing lower back pain and he has stopped them: 'my kettlebell swing form is not the best so it is causing me right some lower back pain so i had to stop that.' Deadlifts also produce lower back pain. He describes a middle back issue as the upstream cause: 'There's a middle back issue as well, which is, by the way, causing the lower back issue, which is also causing some hip issues.' Chronic stiffness attributed to years of bodybuilding. No formal diagnosis stated, no clinician named, and he intends to engage a local physio. Working with a nutrition practitioner locally; follows a low-fat, vegetable-heavy Mediterranean diet.

signals: High intent and no price resistance whatsoever — engaged with $6,000/6mo, $9,000/12mo and CHF/EUR conversions without a single affordability remark
The blocker is entirely physical: 'How much can you adjust for injuries? That's a bit the tricky one.'
Pre-emptively questions his own suitability: 'I might not be even like a good fit, right, for this without any issues'
Sets an exit condition on the body, not the money: 'if I'm not feeling comfortable throughout it, then I just need to stop, right, and then find something else'
Wants to run a written list of his conditions past the coach before committing — a clinical-fit gate, not a financial one
Not fully the archetype in that no clinician has actually ruled anything out; he has not yet been assessed, which is itself the finding

goals.text: Translate essentially all of his training into kettlebell and bodyweight work he can do at home in a compact space
Build correct form and a proper foundation so he stops injuring himself — the explicit reason he is buying coaching
Resolve the stiffness accumulated from years of bodybuilding, and the interlinked mid-back, lower-back and hip issues
Make this his main form of exercise for the next decade or more, adapting as he ages, rather than chasing heavy weight
Train efficiently in the early-morning window his young child leaves him
Use circuit-style conditioning to move his heart rate up and down and flush stress

pains.text: Kettlebell swings are currently causing lower back pain and he has had to stop doing them; deadlifts do the same
Middle back issue driving the lower back issue and in turn hip issues
Years of bodybuilding produced escalating stiffness, so training and mobility work were pulling against each other — 'pain in the fitness, and then pain to unpack it'
CrossFit had too much going on and too little attention on form, which created injuries
Free time collapsed by a young child; gym travel time is no longer viable
Cannot take on multiple new systems at once — 'it's just too much mental energy'
Yoga gave him mobility but no real training stimulus
Ageing making stiffness progressively worse — 'age, you know, is not a very nice mistress'

objections.raw_quote: So, uh, fine. Okay. Let me, so, you know, Maybe, so, is there a way for you to check to offload the nutrition out of it or just reconsider it as part of the thing, right?
objections.rep_response: Refused outright — 'Yeah.' — holding the position he had already stated, that the three pillars are a single system and the coaching is not worth buying piecemeal.

objections.raw_quote: How much can you adjust for injuries? That's a bit the tricky one. As I mentioned to there's a bit of a lower back issue. There's a middle back issue as well, which is, by the way, causing the lower back issue, which is also causing some hip issues.
objections.rep_response: Disclosed his own scoliosis to build relatability, asserted broad experience — 'we've worked with loads of people with loads of issues' — and reduced perceived risk by recommending the $1,200 one-month term instead. Did not ask whether any clinician had assessed or cleared him, did not ask for a diagnosis history or duration, and did not suggest getting cleared before starting loaded work.

objections.raw_quote: you know, I might still need some local support if that makes sense You know, through just to, you know, be a bit more focused on certain things. So I'm hoping maybe the two things together, right, would really build it up.
objections.rep_response: Dismissed the need for in-person form checking — 'if we couldn't master the form online, we wouldn't have any good results' — and later argued that keeping a physio and a nutritionist alongside the coaching would make it not worth buying.

objections.raw_quote: I really don't want to do new plans. I don't want to check in right on nutrition. I don't want to check in, you know, on weight.
objections.rep_response: Later reframed the weekly check-in as a progression reference rather than a weight check — 'If you don't want to check in with the weight and stuff, that's fine... you're supposed to progress every week in any area, not just more weight' — which the prospect accepted.

objections.raw_quote: it's always a bit annoying when I onboard a nutritionist, you know, that's like very, what is it, primal, right? You know, based on red meat and eggs, you know, I'm basically cutting all those things out, right? So, not that I'm vegan, right? But, you know, it's very low-fat what I do and what I need to do
objections.rep_response: Cited vegan and Indian vegetarian clients and Trevor's own background — 'We're not going to make you eat red meat if you don't want to eat red meat' — and promised tailoring.

objections.raw_quote: And then, in any case, gear went until, like, the weekend, right? So I cleared my thoughts. So there's no urgency on your side. So you can even come... back to me next week, right, if that's okay.
objections.rep_response: Accepted the delay without any attempt at the think-about-it play; agreed to a WhatsApp follow-up and repeated his recommendation of the one-month term.

offer.guarantee_mentioned: No guarantee or refund was offered. The nearest thing was the one-month term branded as 'love it or leave it' — 'you're committing to one month, you're not committing to three months or six months. You commit to one and then after the first month, we have a meeting' — plus an upgrade-credit statement, 'if you decide to continue, it's not like you have to pay, you just take it off the balance.'

evidence: No close was attempted, no payment taken and no payment link sent
Prospect set his own timeline and explicitly removed urgency: 'there's no urgency on your side. So you can even come back to me next week'

Next step is a written list of his medical issues for Trevor to assess suitability: 'I can maybe tell you in a few bullets the things I'm facing, and then you can check if that's something you guys can gear for or no'

Counter-evidence toward a live deal: strong engagement throughout, extensive mechanics questions, no price resistance at any point, and he explicitly rejected the cheap self-guided alternative — 'I don't think I want to do self things'

Counter-evidence toward a loss: the rep twice told him the full coaching was probably not right for him, and the prospect's own exit condition is physical — 'if I'm not feeling comfortable throughout it, then I just need to stop'
outcome.next_step: Prospect to send a bulleted list of his back and hip issues by WhatsApp that evening or the next day; rep to forward it to Trevor for a suitability read; rep to text him on WhatsApp immediately after the call. Decision expected after the weekend.

notable.note: The most consequential moment is at 00:09:51, where the rep tells a prospect with active spinal pain that the coaching 'wouldn't be worth it if you still had a nutritionist and still had the physio' — steering him away from local clinical support in order to protect the bundle. No one asked whether a clinician had assessed his back before recommending loaded kettlebell work, on a call where the prospect stated that swings are currently causing him lower back pain. Separately, the rep quoted five different prices in three currencies, improvised the Swiss franc conversion live and inconsistently ('4.6 K francs. I think' then '4.7 K francs'), and finished by recommending the smallest, unsanctioned $1,200 term. Occupation and income were never asked at any point in a 32-minute qualification call.

quality.notes: Severe and sustained. The block at 00:06:00 is labelled 'Marc Moubarak' but contains the rep's summary and his question 'have you started doing kettlebells yet like at home or no' as well as the prospect's answer. Throughout the process walkthrough from 00:15:04 to 00:22:09 short acknowledgements and continuations are systematically assigned to the wrong speaker — e.g. 'Where do you want to be? Right. In six months time.' is labelled Marc but is the rep, and 'It's called True Coach' is labelled Marc. The price exchange at 00:11:30-00:12:01 is partly inverted, with 'Six months is 4.7 K francs' and 'In USD, it's 6K' both attributable to the rep. All roles resolved from content.
